limits: Python and libraries on this page: the examples run in your browser, in Python 3.13.2 with its standard library and Pyodide's ssl package, while the research ran Python 3.14.6 on Linux with ezgmail 2026.4.28, requests 2.34.2 and aiosmtpd 1.4.6 (none of them is on this page). Each concept example and each chapter example was run in the browser and compared with its recorded result.

Recorded, not run: 36 examples need something a browser's Python cannot give (sockets between programs, a server in a thread, another program, the process time zone) or a library that is not on the page (ezgmail, licence GPLv3+, and Google's client library, a 16.8 MB wheel), or print what Python 3.14 added to imaplib and Python 3.13 does not have; each is shown with its output recorded under Python 3.14.6, labelled 'Recorded, not run on this page', with its reason: AppendixAnswers, AttachmentNames, AttachmentParts, BodyEncoding, CcAndBccHeaders, CertificateVerification, CommandInjectionRefused, CredentialsAndToken, DeprecatedOauthLibrary, DownloadOverwrite, EmailControlLoop, EnvelopeRecipients, EnvelopeVersusHeader, ExampleDates, FilenameTraversal, ImapIdle, ImapParsing, ImportRunsInit, ListingsReplay, LoginAfterTls, MessageFields, MetadataHeaders, NewlineInHeader, NonAsciiText, PollUrl, PostBody, QuotedTextCut, RefusedRecipients, ReplyThreading, ResponseObject, SendCall, StarttlsSession, SummaryLine, ThreadVersusMessage, TokenFileContents, UnreadRecentSearch.

No real Gmail account, phone, ntfy server or Twilio account was reached, anywhere. Programs of the recording ran against local stand-ins and say so: the real ezgmail and the real Google library against a replacement of Google's HTTP object whose replies were written by the study, a local SMTP server (aiosmtpd) with a self-signed certificate, a local IMAP server (dovecot 2.3.21), a recorder in place of ntfy, a list of messages in place of a mailbox, a sample forecast and a page of HTML written for the course. Their output shows what the libraries send and how the program reacts, not what Gmail, a phone company, ntfy or weather.gov answers.

No wheel is embedded on this page and no file of the book's online materials (a zip of 7,759,877 bytes, none of its files is about this chapter); ezgmail is licensed GPLv3+ and Google's client library is a 16.8 MB wheel, so both are only recorded (03-materials/ch20/assets/ASSETS_PROVENANCE_v1_0_0.md).

NOT EXECUTED: any Gmail account, Google Cloud project, OAuth consent screen, browser authorisation or token refresh (so the 7-day expiry of a Testing refresh token, the acceptance of .exe and .zip attachments by Gmail and the behaviour of a real inbox are read, not run); a connection to Gmail's servers (imap.gmail.com and smtp.gmail.com timed out from this machine); any text message (no phone number, carrier, gateway delivery or Twilio account; Twilio's API was only asked once without credentials and answered 401); any publication to ntfy.sh, the ntfy app and the real ntfy server (github.com answered 403 and archive.heckel.io was denied, so no ntfy binary; ntfy.sh was only asked for its health and for the messages of an unused topic); Windows and macOS (the Popen of qBittorrent and a torrent download); the 153 and 67 character segments of long texts, which come from arithmetic and were not found on a page opened by this study; Python 3.14.7 and later and the final 3.15.0 (uv offered 3.15.0b4); the commit the course pins; and a photograph (the single request to Wikimedia Commons answered 429).

What the public sites answered on 2026-10-13 is in live_observations_v1_0_0.json: the chapter's page (status 200, 53,147 bytes, equal to the digest in the book's ontology), the notices of AT&T and Verizon, ntfy.sh (health 200, {"healthy":true}; a poll of an unused topic, nothing published), Twilio's API asked once without credentials (status 401) and the DNS answers for the 18 gateway domains of Table 20-1, of which 12 have mail exchangers (MX records); sms.cricketwireless.net answered only name aliases (CNAME). A missing MX is a symptom, not proof that delivery fails.

One program was run under 11 interpreters (3.11.17, 3.12.3, 3.13.16, 3.14.0, 3.14.1, 3.14.2, 3.14.3, 3.14.4, 3.14.5, 3.14.6, 3.15.0b4); the 19 items that differ between them are listed in interpreter_record_v1_0_0.json (for example imaplib's idle() from Python 3.14, the lower case mail from: and rcpt to: that smtplib sends from Python 3.13, the removed keyfile and certfile arguments, and the verify flags of ssl.create_default_context() that Python 3.13 added; its TLS 1.2 minimum is older: 3.11.17 already reports it, the documentation dates it to 3.10, and the Ubuntu 3.12.3 package reports the lowest supported version). The book's Appendix A pins requests 2.32.3; the 8 items of the third-party record were run with the newest releases and with that pin.
